headline: Exercise is movement that strengthens—your body adapts to demands placed upon it
universal_truth: Bodies are built to move; use your capacity or lose it; what you don't use atrophies
fun_facts: Regular exercise reduces all-cause mortality by about 30%
Your brain grows new neurons during exercise—it's not just physical
Hunter-gatherers walked about 10 miles per day—our bodies evolved for movement
discussion_questions: How much are you moving compared to what your body expects?
What happens when you don't move enough?
What movement could you add that you'd actually enjoy?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Your ancestors walked 10 miles daily, lifted heavy things, ran from predators. Your body expects movement. When you don't move, it interprets stillness as illness and starts shutting down. Movement isn't optional—it's required.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We know exercise is good, yet most people don't do enough. What makes movement so essential?

options.text: Bodies adapt to demands—they maintain capacity for what you do regularly and discard what you don't use; not moving signals 'don't need this' and capacity shrinks
options.response: Yes. Your body is efficient—it maintains only what you use. Stop moving, and it stops maintaining movement capacity. Use it or lose it isn't just a saying—it's biology.
Calories matter, but the deeper issue is capacity maintenance—your body adapts to demands...

q1.title: Adaptation to Demands
q1.script: Muscles grow when challenged. Bones strengthen under load. Hearts improve with cardio demands. Your body builds capacity for what you ask it to do—and removes capacity for what you don't.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Adaptation to Demands"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Beyond Physical
q2.script: Exercise isn't just physical—it improves mood, reduces anxiety, sharpens thinking. Your brain grows new neurons during movement. Mental and physical health are connected.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Minimum Effective Dose
q3.script: You don't need hours. Even 20 minutes of movement triggers adaptation. Walking counts. Consistency beats intensity. The best exercise is the one you'll actually do.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Bodies are built to move. Use your capacity or lose it. What you don't use atrophies. Move regularly.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 303. Tomorrow, we'll explore building stronger muscles—strength training. Until then, add some movement to your day.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Movement Audit - How Much Do You Move?
growTrack.learning_objective: Assess current movement and plan improvements
growTrack.activity: How much do you move in a typical day? Walking, exercise, physical activity? Is it enough to maintain the capacity you want? What one addition would improve your movement pattern?
